transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood), Anya Chen (Redwood SE), Maya S. (CTO), Ethan P. (Lead ML), Liam O. (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on self-serve quickstart, how long until first token, trial credits and if Dedicated or Private will be needed in 90 days.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Anya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Maya: Doing good, thanks. Quick agenda — we want to understand your quickstart, the free credits, and at a high level what it would take to run some embeddings and a chat POC.
[00:12] Jordan: Great, that's perfect. I'll start with the PLG flow and free credits then Anya will jump into latency, batch-ing and what to expect for dedicated etc.
[00:20] Anya: Hi all. On the quickstart side you can get an API key and hit the hosted API in minutes. We have SDK samples in python, node, and a curl example — usually "time to first token" is sub-5 minutes for devs who have git and curl ready. 
[00:30] Ethan: Quick question, when you say API key creation, is that self-serve from console or do we need a sales touch to enable trial credits?
[00:37] Jordan: Self-serve — you can sign up, get a free tier and credits. For trials that map to a POC we can bump credits for you, that's what the AE does. We'll share details on limits — like X tokens/day default, and bump policy.
[00:50] Liam: What's the friction to get streaming responses working? We have a chat flow where UX depends on low first-token latency.
[00:57] Anya: Streaming is supported out of the box on hosted. For low-first-token we recommend small prompt prefix caching, and for chat we use KV cache to avoid re-computing. There's some transcription hiccup here — sometimes the docs say KV cache as K V cache but it's the same concept.
[01:14] Maya: We're evaluating whether hosted is enough vs reserved/dedicated. In 3 months we may need to push to Dedicated for consistent throughput and SLA. What's the threshold?
[01:22] Jordan: Common pattern — start on hosted for dev and early POC, then move to Dedicated when you need predictable throughput or isolation. Usually teams hit Dedicated conversations when sustained QPS and latency SLOs matter, or when policy requires tenant isolation. We'll give rough guidance later in the call.
[01:35] Ethan: Security: we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. Can the hosted flow comply?
[01:42] Anya: Hosted customers get SOC2 controls in the platform; we also have KMS integrations for Private deployments. Hosted has encryption at rest and in transit and audit logs, but for customer-managed keys and VPC you would look at Private. We do have an enterprise hosted option with stricter controls — and we can share the security pack.
[02:00] Liam: On latency/cost, can you ballpark embed cost and chat cost for say 1M tokens a month?
[02:07] Jordan: Ballparks are in the pricing sheet but rough: embeddings are usually cheaper per unit, chat generation cost depends on model and quantization. We recommend running a small benchmark — it's the fastest way to see unit economics. We'll share a sample benchmark spreadsheet.
[02:25] Maya: For the quickstart, what's the easiest path to validate embeddings quality and speed?
[02:30] Anya: Use the embeddings quickstart notebook — it's a one-click in our repo. Pull sample data, call embeddings endpoint, then run similarity queries. For speed, run on hosted first, if you see tail latencies you can ask Anya for a dedicated perf run.
[02:47] Ethan: Do you have pre-selected models for embeddings and chat?
[02:52] Jordan: Yes, we publish a model catalog with verified performance profiles. For embeddings we'll point to a few curated models with performance tradeoffs. Some of the names get munged in transcripts — you'll see model names like redwood-ann-embed in docs.
[03:06] Maya: If we want to keep data in our VPC, what's the time and lift to go to Private?
[03:12] Anya: Private has a longer lead time — typically 6-10 weeks depending on infra and network work. If you need VPC peering + KMS integration it's more setup than hosted. But a common path is: hosted for POC, Dedicated reserved capacity for scale, Private for regulatory/data-residency.
[03:29] Liam: For the POC, do we need to sign any DPA?
[03:33] Jordan: We have a standard DPA and can provide it pre-sign. For POC it's often fine to proceed under the standard terms and then escalate procurement when you move to Dedicated/Private.
[03:42] Ethan: Can you share the quickstart curl example now?
[03:45] Jordan: Sure, I'll paste one in the follow-up, but basically: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"Hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate — the SDKs wrap that. We also have streaming via SSE and WebSocket examples.
[04:05] Maya: We care about SSO for our team. Does the console support SCIM and SAML?
[04:10] Anya: Yes, enterprise accounts support SAML/SCIM provisioning and RBAC. For self-serve you can use basic invite flows, but enterprise SSO requires an account tier upgrade.
[04:20] Liam: We might want to test end-to-end within 2 weeks. Is that realistic?
[04:24] Jordan: Definitely. If you sign up today, get an API key, run the quickstart and then we can widen credits. First token within minutes, full mini-POC in a few days.
[04:34] Ethan: What about rate limits on the trial? If our embed pipeline sends bursts, will we get throttled?
[04:39] Anya: Trials have conservative defaults, but we can temporarily raise limits for a POC. For production you can configure autoscaling with Dedicated or set burst policies. There's also prefix caching and batching to reduce costs.
[04:53] Maya: Any gotchas for Golang or Rust SDKs? Most examples are node/python.
[04:58] Jordan: We have community-supported SDKs for Go and Rust, official ones for python/node. If you need a sample snippet we'll include one in the follow-up.
[05:08] Liam: Regarding billing and quotas — can we map usage to teams and projects in the console?
[05:13] Anya: Yes, project-and-route level reporting, token-level cost breakdowns, and tagging so you can allocate spend.
[05:20] Maya: If we want Dedicated in the future, can we reserve capacity quickly?
[05:24] Jordan: Dedicated requires a capacity reservation and some lead time, but we do offer burst modes and can do short-term capacity commitments while you evaluate. We'll propose options based on your expected QPS.
[05:36] Ethan: For security review, who would we talk to at Redwood?
[05:39] Jordan: I'll introduce you to our security lead and solutions architect; Anya will route security docs — SOC2 report, pen-test summary, architecture diagrams.
[05:47] Maya: Sounds good. Can you walk us through a hypothetical bench: embeddings 100k queries/day, chat 50 reqs/min with 2s p95?
[05:56] Anya: Sure, for those numbers hosted often suffices, but p95 depends on model size and quantization. If 2s p95 is a hard SLO, we recommend Dedicated with pinned model variants and autoscaling. We'll also suggest batching strategies and whether to enable KV prefix caching.
[06:16] Jordan: Quick note on costs — quantized variants and smaller models will save you a lot. Our Optimize tool will recommend quantization and batching settings based on your workload.
[06:26] Liam: Do you have example accounts where customers started hosted then moved to Dedicated?
[06:29] Jordan: Yep, many. We can share anonymized case studies — e.g., one FinTech started hosted for dev and 6 months later took Dedicated for SLA and VPC.
[06:38] Maya: Okay what's next?
[06:40] Jordan: I'll send the quickstart guide, curl examples, free credit details and the benchmark spreadsheet. Anya will schedule a technical deep-dive to measure latencies and go over embeddings. Customer to try quickstart and share initial numbers.
[06:51] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone.
[06:54] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
